judged_text: The findFirst-then-create sequence is a check-then-insert race with no UNIQUE(userId, appId) constraint backing it (the in-code claim that upsert is impossible is exactly the missing unique key), and the (userId, appId) slot also has a second writer in the local OAuth callback. Two concurrent webhook deliveries (e.g., a reconnect racing an in-flight sync) both miss the findFirst and create duplicate Credential rows for the same user and app, and the findFirst can also overwrite the key of a locally-installed credential; consumers binding to a stale duplicate use dead tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, credentials are written using a non-atomic `findFirst` then `create` sequence keyed by `{ userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }`. This is inherently racy: two concurrent requests can both observe no row and both execute `prisma.credential.create(...)`, producing duplicate credential rows unless the DB enforces a UNIQUE constraint on `(userId, appId)` (no such constraint is shown in this diff), and there is no retry/unique-violation handling. Even if a unique constraint exists, this code would still intermittently 500 on concurrent deliveries. The comment “Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id” further suggests the code is not relying on a unique key, increasing the likelihood of duplicates.
